_about: Level-0 concept index. Each concept is an ABSTRACT craft feature (no copyrighted text), a concise card, and — critically — a `used_by` link naming the deterministic check, agent, or skill that consumes it. A concept with no `used_by` is inert and should not be here. Cards draw on two source streams (see kb/source-register.json `stream`): CRAFT-INSTRUCTION (writing tutorials/poetics, many public-domain) for heuristics, and FICTION-CORPUS for pattern analysis. Every concept also carries STRUCTURED DEPTH (ADR 0015): a one-line `claim`, an `evidence_strength` grade (structural | craft-heuristic | theoretical | contested | empirical), `dangerous_when` conditions where the card misleads, `counterexamples`, and resolvable `conflicts_with` links — so a card can never be an inert or over-absolute rule. `validate_workspace.py` verifies every card file exists, every source id is registered, and every concept carries that depth with resolvable conflicts.

concepts.use_when: Any time a problem might be causal (what happens) vs. presentational (how it is told).
concepts.claim: Separate what happens (fabula) from how it is told (discourse); route a defect to one layer, not both.
concepts.dangerous_when: Treating discourse (reading) order as fabula (event) order — flashbacks/parallel timelines need explicit event-time.
counterexamples: a frame narrative where the discourse order is itself the meaning

concepts.use_when: Planning or auditing whether an event can happen yet.
concepts.claim: An event can occur only if its preconditions already hold (actors present, objects available, prior events done).
concepts.dangerous_when: Over-constraining forms that reject strict causal closure (dream logic, absurdism).
counterexamples: surrealist fiction where causality is deliberately broken

concepts.use_when: Deciding or testing whether an action follows from a character rather than the plot.
concepts.claim: An action should follow from a character's beliefs/desires/values, not from plot convenience.
concepts.dangerous_when: Characters swept by forces beyond agency (disaster, reflex, shock) legitimately act without full intention.
counterexamples: a character in shock acting on reflex, not decision

concepts.use_when: Choosing/auditing whose perception filters a scene and who knows what.
concepts.claim: A scene is filtered through a focalizer who knows only what they have learned; knowledge must not leak from the future or another mind.
concepts.dangerous_when: The current state model treats knowledge as MONOTONIC — it cannot represent forgetting, misremembering, false belief, or revised belief; do not rely on it for amnesia or unreliable-narrator plots.
counterexamples: an unreliable narrator who believes a false 'fact'
a character who forgets what they knew

concepts.use_when: Opening a reader expectation, or checking whether one was paid off.
concepts.claim: A raised reader expectation must be paid off or deliberately, visibly refused.
concepts.dangerous_when: Deliberate non-payoff (anti-climax, open ending) is a valid contract, not always a defect.
counterexamples: a modernist open ending that withholds resolution on purpose

concepts.use_when: Writing a scene spec or judging whether a scene is necessary.
concepts.claim: A scene turns: a value shifts as desire meets conflict — 'if nothing changes, it is not a scene' (McKee/Swain).
concepts.dangerous_when: Lyric, modernist, observational, or deliberately anticlimactic fiction whose force is voice/texture/perception, not a value turn.
counterexamples: a static lyric scene that grips through perceptual precision (see static-scene)

concepts.use_when: Writing or auditing dialogue; testing conflict beneath the words.
concepts.claim: Dialogue carries conflict beneath the words; characters pursue tactics and rarely state their real aim.
concepts.dangerous_when: On-the-nose speech can be right for characters who are blunt, panicked, ritualistic, or plain-spoken.
counterexamples: a flat declaration at a moment where subtext would falsify the character

concepts.use_when: Scheduling information; judging whether a surprise is earned.
concepts.claim: Manage what the reader knows vs. the characters to produce suspense (reader knows more), surprise (less), or curiosity (a gap).
concepts.dangerous_when: Manufacturing a gap by withholding what the focalizer plainly would know (authorial cheating).
counterexamples: a story whose power is total transparency, nothing withheld

concepts.use_when: Tuning how close the prose sits to a character's consciousness.
concepts.claim: Prose can sit anywhere from panoramic report to deep interiority; distance should move with intent, not drift.
concepts.dangerous_when: Fixing a single distance dogmatically; some voices thrive on rapid, deliberate distance shifts.
counterexamples: free indirect style that glides distance mid-sentence

concepts.use_when: Diagnosing generic, abstract, or ornamental prose.
concepts.claim: Perception lands through concrete, specific detail; abstraction and generic emotion words dilute it.
concepts.dangerous_when: Some registers (aphorism, essayistic fiction, summary) require abstraction as their voice.
counterexamples: an essayistic narrator whose abstraction is the point

concepts.use_when: Detecting model-default phrasing and predictable continuations.
concepts.claim: Model-default phrasing (cliché, told emotion, filter verbs) marks unrevised output; only motivated deviation earns its place.
concepts.dangerous_when: Deliberate cliché (parody, characterization, free-indirect voice) is not a defect, and the regex linter cannot tell the difference.
counterexamples: a character who thinks in clichés, rendered on purpose

concepts.use_when: Shaping act/sequence structure; testing for reversal and recognition.
concepts.claim: Complication and unraveling around reversal (peripeteia) and recognition (anagnorisis) shape a unified action (Aristotle/Freytag).
concepts.dangerous_when: Imposing a five-act arc on forms that reject it (vignette, mosaic, slice-of-life).
counterexamples: a mosaic novel with no single arc

concepts.use_when: Deciding scene vs. summary; diagnosing flat or bloated rendering.
concepts.claim: Render in scene what must be felt; summarize what only needs to be known — telling is a tool, not a sin.
concepts.dangerous_when: The 'never tell' dogma; good summary and direct statement are frequently the right choice.
counterexamples: a told summary that rightly compresses years into a sentence

concepts.use_when: Judging scene necessity and coherence of a short work to its intended affect.
concepts.claim: In a short work every element should serve one intended affect (Poe); cut what does not.
concepts.dangerous_when: Novels and deliberately digressive forms prize multiplicity over single-effect unity.
counterexamples: a picaresque whose pleasure is its detours

concepts.use_when: Testing whether a beat earns telling (the anti-boredom check).
concepts.claim: A narratable event is a significant, script-deviating change that matters to someone (Labov tellability, Hühn eventfulness).
concepts.dangerous_when: Lyric, static, observational, ritual, or modernist fiction whose force is voice, texture, pattern, or slow perceptual transformation — low eventfulness there is not boredom.
counterexamples: a plotless observational sketch that grips through perceptual precision
a ritual/repetition piece whose sameness is the point

concepts.use_when: Running the story's own PDCA revision loop after any critique.
concepts.claim: Revision is targeted repair checked against the audits: accept only improvement without material regression, and stop rather than drift toward the evaluator's blandness.
concepts.dangerous_when: Over-revising toward an evaluator's preferences can sand off a living voice; the loop must be able to stop.
counterexamples: a rough-but-alive draft that further revision would flatten

concepts.claim: Not every compelling scene turns a value; lyric/static/observational scenes hold on perception, voice, pattern, or ritual and derive force from precision, not change.
concepts.use_when: Judging a scene that seems not to 'turn' — before flagging it inert, decide whether it is a deliberate static mode the contract allows.
concepts.dangerous_when: Using it to excuse a genuinely inert scene under a contract that promised eventful drama.
counterexamples: a 'static' scene that is merely an errand with no perceptual charge — that one IS inert

concepts.claim: In this repo's worked example, the decision scene turns through the hands — the near-call, the phone set down, the watched second scald, the kneading rhythm — dramatizing an agency shift without naming feeling.
concepts.use_when: As a concrete model of enacting a character decision through action, and of a scene that turns on a status/agency shift rather than an external event.
concepts.dangerous_when: It is one sample; do not induce a universal rule from it (AGENTS.md: never learn a style rule from a single success).
